question: While designing a Claude-assisted tender-summary arrangement, an analyst finds that every draft needs the same three corrections. Which response is most appropriate?
options: A) Keep making the three corrections by hand, since they take only a minute
B) Move to a more capable model, which should stop the corrections recurring
C) Fold those three corrections into the written instructions and try again
D) Ask for three separate drafts each time and pick whichever needs least work
correct_answers: C) Fold those three corrections into the written instructions and try again
explanations: Hand-correcting works while one person runs it, but the fix vanishes the moment anyone else uses the arrangement.
A stronger model cannot infer three unstated requirements, so the same three corrections will keep appearing.
Correct. A repeated correction is a specification the instruction is missing. Writing it in makes the fix part of the design instead of something the analyst re-applies every time.
Generating extra drafts increases the work of choosing without addressing why every draft has the same gap.
